summary.intent: Resume Caliper work that Claude Code left unfinished at the weekly usage limit (lazy-session chained dependency index, confidence-score experiment, shadcn/antd prop gaps), then close remaining prop gaps and hardening in properly stacked PRs with green CI.
summary.outcome: Chained-layer loader fix and several prop-gap extractor fixes were opened as stacked PRs (#203-#207+), confidence experiment concluded no-go, and a Changesets/Callisto CI fix was propagated so 18 of 19 open PRs ended green. The user lost trust after repeated premature 'fixed' claims, miscounts, a duplicate-enum compile error, and an unnecessary PR (#221 draft/publish approach), and ended the session angry and downgrading.

repo: PRs are stacked (#200 -> #203, #201 -> #204 -> #205 -> #206 -> #207 ... #220); base-branch fixes do not propagate to descendants automatically and must be merged down in stack order.

Caliper's Changesets CI job runs Callisto 0.12; CARGO_TERM_COLOR=always injects ANSI codes into Cargo's 'could not find' message, so Callisto misclassifies an absent registry version as an indeterminate provider error (E176). Fix: disable Cargo color in release-planning paths.
Callisto also raises E320 when validating an unversioned PR tree against already-published versions; validation needs a versioned temporary worktree (callisto version + release --dry-run).

The 0.6.0 release published caliper-docgen-core but stopped at the CLI because it depends on caliper-docgen-semantic by path with publish=false; the CLI, npm CLI, NAPI and Storybook packages remain unreleased/at 0.5.0. Resolution (publish deps vs. bundle into CLI vs. stop crates.io publishing) is an undecided distribution choice.
Backend crates ship test helper binaries (fake-tsc, replay-tsc), so simply marking them publishable would publish those too.
Changesets entries should not start with bullets because the generated changelog adds its own bullet, causing '- -' nesting; keep them short, friendly, user-focused.

Public enum variants must be appended, not inserted mid-enum (DetectionRule/MemoExoticDecl insertion shifted discriminants and broke SemVer); adding a public field to FunctionResult needs a minor changeset.
Repo maintenance scripts (parity, equivalence) are Python called from CI and justfile; decision was to keep Python plus Bash rather than migrate to Ruby.
Fresh worktrees lack node_modules, causing insta snapshot path-prefix failures; install locked deps in the worktree to verify snapshots.
Equivalence check uses an allowlist by diff category; intentional output changes need narrowly scoped allowances (no prop removals allowed).

Corpus oracle: TS 7.1 supplies offline labels only; the confidence score uses Caliper-only output signals. Only 1 hard wrong-type across 6 corpora (Spectrum, likely alias-expansion artifact); of shadcn's remaining checker-only props, ~1,154 are Next's `tw` module augmentation via @vercel/og, which needs an import-scope design decision.

Extractor gaps fixed: callable `declare const` components in ComponentProps<typeof X>, imported ReactElement return spelling, lowercase exported values (cmdk), static-member intersections, Vaul namespace objects, input-otp React$1 alias, MemoExoticComponent (streamdown), generic callable type params bound to unknown, and false components from JSX passed as call arguments (e.g. GET returning new ImageResponse(<div/>)).
Explicit forwardRef<Ref,Props> ref-injection probe was rejected: it added 77 ref props to Chakra and 3 to shadcn with no matching historical gap.
workflow: Never report CI/PR state as green without checking the current head SHA and completed (not pending) checks for every open PR; pending/queued is not pass.
When propagating a fix through a stack, build/compile each descendant head (merging an enum fix left two MemoExoticDecl variants and broke the release build).
Batch-pushing across a stack triggers many CI runs and email noise; validate locally (actionlint, callisto status/version/dry-run) first and push once per branch.
Before opening a PR that expands the public release surface (e.g. publishing internal crates), compare alternatives and get a decision first.
Courier commit/PR skills require explicit approval of exact commit message, scope and PR body before committing.

friction: User was repeatedly told things were fixed or green when CI was still red or pending (at least five times), eroding trust.
Miscounted failing PRs several times (14 vs 13 vs 19 open PRs, 11 vs 13) and initially missed #214 entirely.
Merge propagation introduced a duplicate MemoExoticDecl variant that broke the release build on #218-#220.
#221 was opened as a publish-two-crates fix that was unnecessary, would have shipped test helper binaries, and could not clear Changesets alone; it was also marked draft against the user's wishes.
Opened another PR (#222) while the release blocker was unresolved, and triggered many CI runs and failure emails.
Weekly rate limit killed three Claude background agents mid-work; worktrees were also partially deleted by outside cleanup.
Local environment issues: read-only Cargo cache broke a first Callisto run, worktrees lacked node_modules causing snapshot failures, and CLI watch integration tests timed out locally.
Slow queued GitHub Actions made waiting per-branch for full CI impractical.
open_items: Generated release PR #217 has no checks, is UNSTABLE, and lacks the #221 manifest fix; it should not be merged as is.
Decide how to finish the incomplete 0.6.0 release (CLI absent from crates.io; npm packages still 0.5.0) and whether to keep `cargo install caliper-docgen` via publishing deps or bundling the backend.
Seven snapshot failures from path prefixes in the chained-layer worktree remained unverified for the full snapshot suite.
Next's `tw` module augmentation (1,154 shadcn props) needs a design for import-scope-aware augmentation handling and watch updates.
Spectrum `ref` rows and antd `SubMenu` and Mantine polymorphic factory extras remain unresolved; ref handling needs wrapper-type tracing.
PR #202's architecture documentation needed updating for the on-by-default dependency loading; ADR index merged with ADR 0020.
The confidence-score experiment is a no-go for automatic fallback; script and report were published as a separate PR but need further label separation.
Remaining CI cause for #218-#220 git failures was never proven; they passed after the workflow change.
Open PRs #202, #219, #220, #222 were still finishing non-Changesets checks at the last pass; #222 (changeset copy cleanup) remains blocked on the release state.
Copy polish of the four pending 0.6 changesets on main and the authoring rule were in #222.
